claim: Popular code generation benchmarks show substantial surface-level and semantic-level overlap with open pretraining corpora such as RedPajama-Data-1T and StarCoder-Data.
stance_target: popular code benchmarks (e.g. HumanEval, MBPP) being clean, uncontaminated evaluation sets for measuring genuine model capability or confidence discrimination
scope_conditions: popular code generation benchmarks vs. open pretraining corpora, surface and semantic matching pipeline
quoted_support: we show that there are substantial overlap between popular code generation benchmarks and open training corpus, and models perform significantly better on the subset of the benchmarks where similar solutions are seen during training.

claim: Models perform significantly better on the subset of code benchmark problems where similar solutions were present in their training data, indicating benchmark scores conflate memorization with generalization.
stance_target: code-LLM benchmark performance metrics (and by extension confidence-discrimination metrics computed on the same benchmarks) are inflated by data contamination
scope_conditions: comparison of model accuracy on contaminated vs. non-contaminated benchmark subsets
quoted_support: models perform significantly better on the subset of the benchmarks where similar solutions are seen during training.

claim: Model memorization vs. generalization on code benchmarks is modulated by model size, problem difficulty, and question length.
stance_target: which factors predict contamination-driven performance inflation in code LLMs
scope_conditions: factor analysis across contamination matching pipeline results
quoted_support: We also conduct extensive analysis on the factors that affects model memorization and generalization, such as model size, problem difficulty, and question length.
